title: [Web] Text input is placed with an offset above the keyboard when focused
body: I created a simple Flutter web app with an editable field at the bottom of the screen. On mobile browsers, tapping the field opens the keyboard, but the app content is moved too far upward and leaves extra space between the field and the keyboard. I can reproduce it with a CanvasKit web build on physical iPhones and Android devices. The field should align directly above the keyboard. I am using Flutter stable 3.7.9 and have included minimal sample code and a hosted reproduction.

symptoms_visible: On a Flutter web page, focusing the blue editable field opens the mobile keyboard but leaves extra blank space between the keyboard and the app content instead of aligning the field directly above it.
N0.label: N0 mobile keyboard offset reported

symptoms_visible: Changing Scaffold's resizeToAvoidBottomInset behavior does not remove the extra space in the reporter's reproduction; the whole mobile web view still appears to move when the keyboard opens.
N1_x.label: N1_x resize setting aftermath

symptoms_visible: The extra keyboard gap occurs on physical iPhone 14, iPhone X, and Samsung S22 Ultra devices; an HTML-renderer build shows the same result as CanvasKit, while Android reproduction can be intermittent.
N2.label: N2 devices and renderers ruled in

symptoms_visible: Repeated tapping eventually produces the gap on Android Chrome and occasionally on iOS; it is more frequent in complex or scrollable pages when a focused field must be moved upward for the keyboard.
Affected users report the content sometimes moving as if keyboard space were applied twice, including for standard dialogs and fields that are not exactly at the bottom.
N3.label: N3 intermittent cross-device reproduction established

symptoms_visible: After dismissing the Android virtual keyboard with its own control, the reported Flutter geometry changes from a 770-pixel-tall view with a 312-pixel bottom inset to a 458-pixel-tall view with a negative 312-pixel bottom inset; programmatic defocus restores normal geometry.
N4.label: N4 invalid post-keyboard geometry measured

symptoms_visible: On the fixed Flutter release and current master, affected users can open and dismiss the keyboard without the extra white space or incorrect text-field offset on real mobile devices.
One Android web verification uses resizeToAvoidBottomInset disabled for the Scaffold, while other users also confirm the updated Flutter installation works.
N5.label: N5 patched builds verified

symptoms_visible: The Flutter web geometry fix is available in stable 3.38.6 and later; reporters confirm that focusing, closing, and reopening mobile keyboards no longer leaves the erroneous gap after updating.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved in stable Flutter

solution.intent: Treat the gap as ordinary Scaffold keyboard resizing and change resizeToAvoidBottomInset.
solution.concrete_example: Set Scaffold(resizeToAvoidBottomInset: false), or otherwise change that property, so the Scaffold does not resize when the keyboard appears.

edges.comment: The reporter had already tried the property without resolving the issue, and many later affected users reported the same. A platform-specific resize setting may still be needed by an individual app after the framework fix, but it is not the root fix or a universal resolution.

question_patterns: Does this happen on physical devices or only in a simulator?
Which phones and operating-system versions reproduce the gap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It also happens on physical iPhone 14, iPhone X, and Samsung S22 Ultra devices. The iPhones are on iOS 16 or later. Android reproduction is rarer, but it is visible on a physical device.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens in one simulator and never on any physical phone.
It reproduces on a different recent iPhone and Android model than those originally listed.

question_patterns: Can you build with the HTML renderer and compare it with CanvasKit?
Is the behavior specific to the CanvasKit renderer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created an HTML-renderer build and got the same result. The issue therefore occurs with both HTML and CanvasKit. Here is an Android capture showing the extra space.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The HTML build works every time and only CanvasKit shows the gap.

edges.comment: Physical-device and renderer checks are measurements. They establish that the report is not simulator-only or CanvasKit-only.

question_patterns: Can anyone else reproduce it, and under what interaction or layout conditions?
Does repeated focusing, scrolling, or using another sample make the problem reproducible?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Multiple affected users can reproduce it on Android Chrome and, less consistently, iOS Safari. Repeated taps may be necessary. It is especially frequent in scrollable or more complex pages where the field is in the lower half of the screen, although it can also affect standard date-picker input.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No other user can reproduce it, even after repeatedly testing the hosted sample on the same device models.
The frequency differs by device, but repeated focus and keyboard interactions still produce the same extra gap.
The affected app uses a different color theme.

question_patterns: Is the field required to be at the very bottom, or does it happen whenever the keyboard must move the field?
What is common about the field position when the gap appears?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is not limited to fields exactly at the bottom. It appears whenever a focused field must be pushed upward to remain visible above the keyboard, and can look as though the keyboard offset was applied twice.

question_patterns: Is this isolated to the reporter's application?
Do other users see the same behavior on their devices and applications?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, it affects many separate Flutter web apps and devices. Reports include Pixel, Galaxy, Xiaomi, iPhone, and tablet devices across Chrome, Safari, and other mobile browsers.

edges.comment: Evidence from the reporter and other affected participants is folded into one simulated user side. The screenshots came from cross-platform reproduction in c14.

question_patterns: Can you log the view size and bottom inset before and after dismissing the virtual keyboard?
Does dismissing through the keyboard control produce different geometry from programmatically unfocusing the field?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On Android web, programmatic defocus reports Size(412, 770) with viewInsets.bottom 312 before the geometry settles normally. Dismissing through the keyboard control instead reports Size(412, 458) and viewInsets.bottom -312. The screen remains shortened with a negative inset, matching the visible blank-space behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both dismissal methods restore the full 412 by 770 view with a zero bottom inset, even while the gap remains visible.
The exact keyboard height is different, but dismissal still leaves the view shorter by that height and produces an equal negative bottom inset.

edges.comment: This is the decisive geometry measurement from c100-c101. It links the visible offset to invalid Flutter web metrics after virtual-keyboard dismissal rather than to application padding alone.

question_patterns: Can you update to the release containing PR 179581 and retest the focus, dismiss, and reopen sequence on a real device?
Does the latest stable or master build still leave the extra keyboard gap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The latest published Flutter build works on Chrome on a physical Pixel 8. Other affected users confirm the latest master also resolves the issue, and another clean Flutter installation works correctly. One Android web app needed resizeToAvoidBottomInset disabled in its Scaffold configuration, but the previous erroneous gap is gone.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Stable 3.38.6 and the latest master still produce the same negative inset and extra gap on the physical Pixel device.
The fixed build works on a different physical Android phone and current iOS browser after the same keyboard sequence.

edges.comment: PR 179581 fixed the identical geometry defect tracked in issue 175074 and was cherry-picked to stable 3.38.6. Verification reports from c109-c113 are folded into one user side; the root-cause linkage and release vehicle are engineer-inferred facts used by the final solution.

solution.intent: Resolve the mobile web keyboard offset by using Flutter's framework fix for the invalid post-keyboard viewport geometry, released through PR 179581 in stable 3.38.6, and close only after the affected focus and dismissal sequence is verified on real devices.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Flutter 3.38.6 or later, which contains PR 179581 for the web keyboard geometry bug shared with issue 175074. Rebuild the web app and verify on an affected physical device by focusing the field, dismissing the keyboard with its own control, and reopening it. The view should return to its full height without a negative bottom inset or extra gap. If an Android web app also performs Scaffold resizing, retain the app-specific resizeToAvoidBottomInset configuration needed to avoid double resizing, but do not treat that setting as the framework fix.

edges.comment: The issue was closed after users verified the framework fix on current published and master builds. Stable 3.38.6 is the first explicitly identified stable release containing the cherry-pick.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true root cause as Flutter web retaining incorrect screen geometry around virtual-keyboard dismissal, evidenced by the shortened view and negative bottom inset; it is not merely application padding or a CanvasKit-only rendering problem.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: reproduction on physical iOS and Android devices, the same result with HTML and CanvasKit, and the measured Size(412, 458) with a -312 bottom inset after keyboard-controlled dismissal.
Must identify PR 179581, shared with the geometry defect tracked as issue 175074, and stable Flutter 3.38.6 or later as the framework resolution.

Must not present changing resizeToAvoidBottomInset, switching renderers, moving the field, or avoiding programmatic focus as the universal fix: resizeToAvoidBottomInset already failed for the reporter and these measures were only partial app-specific workarounds.
Must require rebuilding and verifying the focus, keyboard dismissal, and reopen sequence on an affected real device before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter application developer who can provide minimal Dart reproductions, deploy web builds, switch renderers, test physical iOS and Android devices, and report layout metrics, but initially needs framework maintainers to isolate the browser geometry defect.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, direct, and cooperative. Supplies concrete device results and captures when asked, notes intermittent behavior plainly, and rejects suggested workarounds when already tested.
